intuition.title: Why vary feed ratio, temperature and reaction time
intuition.summary: The authors compare metal:Te feed ratio, temperature and duration to study nonstoichiometric telluride phases. They report no obvious difference from Cu:Te 2:1 to 1.5:1 at otherwise unchanged 160 °C/8 h conditions. At lower ratios they describe orthorhombic Cu2.86Te2 and other phases. They propose that hydrazine reduction of metal ions to elemental metal at room temperature may leave reactants unevenly dispersed, contributing to phase diversity. This is the authors' qualitative explanation, not an established mechanism; 1.5:1 is prose context, not a separate tabulated route.
intuition.scope: Source discussion; distinction between tabulated experimental rows and author interpretation is retained.

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Electron transfer from a reductant
general_background.summary: A reducing agent can supply electrons that change the oxidation state of a precursor. Coordination and competing reactions affect how that electron transfer contributes to particle formation.

general_background.title: Solvent and transport
